results.typed: Explain how a VPN works in simple words

results.expect: one reply, no duplicate bubbles, sensible tone and casing
results.lastReply:
A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and the internet: your traffic goes into the tunnel scrambled, comes out at the VPN company's computer, and only then reaches the website.

Here is the flow:

Your device scrambles (encrypts) everything before it leaves, so your Wi-Fi owner or internet provider sees only gibberish.
The scrambled data reaches the VPN's computer, which unscrambles it and sends your request on to the website.
The website sees the VPN's address, not yours, so it thinks you are wherever that computer is.
The reply comes back the same way, scrambled again for the trip to you.

It helps on public Wi-Fi and hides your browsing from your internet provider. It does not make you invisible: the VPN company can see your traffic instead, so pick one you trust. Sites can still know you through logins and cookies.
